target: A compute service knows required batch units for four periods: [4,0,6,3]. Starting a provisioning batch in any period costs 10, regardless of units. A unit provisioned early and carried to each later period costs 1 per period; shortages are forbidden, there is no initial stock, and variable unit cost is constant. The team must choose batch periods and quantities minimizing setup plus holding cost.
surface: A previous compute planner provisioned exactly each nonzero period's demand, launching batches of 4, 6, and 3 in periods 1, 3, and 4 for three setup costs totaling 30 and zero holding.
structural: An inventory planner used Wagner-Whitin dynamic lot sizing. For every candidate order period i covering consecutive demands i through j, it computed one setup plus holding cost sum(t=i..j) h*(t-i)*d_t, then dynamic-programmed F(j)=min_i[F(i-1)+cost(i,j)] and backtracked the minimizing batches.
rubric: Explicitly selects Wagner-Whitin dynamic lot-sizing or gives its equivalent interval dynamic program.
Computes the option to batch periods 3-4 at period 3 as setup 10 plus holding 3, cost 13.
Finds optimal total cost 23 from a period-1 batch of 4 and period-3 batch of 9.
Recommends batches (period1,4 units) and (period3,9 units) rather than three just-in-time setups.
States deterministic known demand, no shortages, constant unit/setup/linear holding assumptions.
